verdict.rationale: Grok Bot ships official desktop apps, documented as .deb, .rpm and AppImage Linux packages and, per the runtime probe, macOS and Windows apps. It also has a documented setting for running commands on the local desktop, but nothing shows global hotkeys or the app seeing the user's screen; the Agent Computer preview shows the Bot's cloud desktop, not the user's. Missing for 10: OS-level/global keyboard shortcuts, access to on-screen content of the user's own display, independent hands-on corroboration of the desktop app.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can use an official desktop app with OS-level shortcuts and access to what is on my screen

citations.quote: a `.deb` package for Debian and Ubuntu, an `.rpm` package for Fedora and RHEL, or an AppImage for other distributions.
You can message a Bot from your phone or desktop, the way you would text someone on your team
Execution on Local Computer controls whether Bots can run commands on the desktop in front of you
Grok Bot is driven through its own apps (macOS/Windows/Linux/iOS/Android)
